keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Colony 1763-1783 with its capital at St. Augustine; the boundary with West Florida was the Apalachicola River. The St. Marys River boundary with Georgia is not on the East Florida page (the Georgia page has the 1763 extension to the St. Marys). No area on the page (the infobox field is blank); the gazetteer shape is about 137,000 km2.

ledger.note: 1763: British East Florida is created. The Royal Proclamation of 7 October 1763 created 'the colonies of West Florida and East Florida'; the Treaty of Paris of 10 February 1763 had Spain cede Florida to Britain, and John Hedges served as acting governor from 20 July 1763 (East Florida page). Most of the Spanish population left for Cuba.

ledger.note: 1783: East Florida returns to Spain. The infobox gives 'Transferred to Spain: 25 November 1783' (Peace of Paris: Great Britain 'ceded the territories of West Florida and East Florida back to Spain'); Spain moved the boundary east to the Suwannee in 1785.

notes: Not a Cliopatria row. Pages: East Florida, Royal Proclamation of 1763 (two; Treaty of Paris and British West Florida pages are cited by the sister dossier). Not on the pages: the colony's area, the St. Marys boundary, the Loyalist influx of 1783-85, any date of taking possession beyond the acting governor's term of 20-30 July 1763. The 1763 extension of Georgia to the St. Marys (Province of Georgia page) is recorded in the thirteen-colonies dossier with spanish-florida as counterpart; it lies at the colony's northern edge. The gazetteer has no East Florida region; the shape is Florida east of -85.0.
